doc_summary: Hubinger announces Anthropic's Alignment Stress-Testing team, whose mandate is to red-team Anthropic's alignment techniques and evaluations and empirically show how they could fail. He stresses stress-testing the whole evaluation process, building more natural model organisms, and guarding against overfitting.

items.claim: prefers stress-testing the entire evaluation and commitment process over only running object-level evaluations because the key risk is that the evaluations themselves are insufficient for the risks at hand.
items.quote: Notably, our goal is not object-level red-teaming or evaluation—e.g. we won’t be the ones running Anthropic’s RSP-mandated evaluations to determine when Anthropic should pause or otherwise trigger concrete safety commitments. Rather, our goal is to stress-test that entire process

items.claim: prefers more natural model organisms, such as ones arising from realistic training pipelines, over artificially constructed ones because demonstrations of failure are more convincing when they could plausibly occur in practice.
items.quote: Building more natural model organisms of misalignment, e.g. finding a training pipeline that we might realistically use that we can show would lead to a concrete misalignment failure.

items.claim: Hold out more natural model organisms as a test set rather than iterating on every artificial one, because iterating on the same examples risks overfitting and weakens the test.
items.quote: we want to be cognizant of the risk of overfitting, and it’ll be our responsibility to determine when it is safe to iterate on improving the ability of our alignment techniques to resolve particular model organisms of misalignment that we produce.

items.claim: prefers treating a null result from serious skeptical red-teaming as only partial reassurance over treating it as a safety guarantee because failing to find danger does not prove absence.
items.quote: And if we don’t find anything extremely dangerous despite a serious and skeptical effort, that is some reassurance, but of course not a guarantee of safety.

items.claim: prefers empirical demonstrations of failure aimed at convincing others over theoretical arguments because the goal is to prove that a pessimistic scenario holds and that strategy must change.
items.quote: our job is to try to prove to Anthropic—and the world more broadly—(if it is in fact true) that we are in a pessimistic scenario, that Anthropic’s alignment plans and strategies won’t work, and that we will need to substantially shift gears.

items.claim: Adversarial, meta-level red-teaming of one's own organization's alignment techniques and evaluations is a central theme, with demonstrations meant to show how strategies could fail.
items.quote: Our mission—and our mandate from the organization—is to red-team Anthropic’s alignment techniques and evaluations, empirically demonstrating ways in which Anthropic’s alignment strategies could fail.

items.claim: Planned next work includes concretely stress-testing ASL-3 evaluations.
Planned next work applies interpretability (dictionary learning) to the Sleeper Agents model organisms to gather evidence beyond behavior.
items.quote: Applying techniques from “Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning” to our “Sleeper Agents” models.
